newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-NEWCOMER NANA BREAKS UP SWISS TRIO.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-NEWCOMER NANA BREAKS UP SWISS TRIO.

text.p: Newcomer Matteo Nana, keeping Italian hopes alive in the absence of world champion Alberto Tomba, staved off a Swiss 1-2-3 in the first leg of a men's Alpine skiing World Cup giant slalom on Sunday.

Swiss World Cup champion Michael von Gruenigen, seeking his first win of the season after a second and third place, started third and clocked the fastest time of one minute 18.15 seconds through the 56 gates on the demanding Gran Risa piste.
That was just 0.02 ahead of his team mate and second starter Steve Locher, winner of the season-opening giant in Soelden, Austria, in October.
Urs Kaelin, second in the last giant slalom in Breckenridge last month. was the fifth skier in action and looked to have completed the Swiss trio at the top with 1:19.34.
But Kaelin had not bargained for 22-year-old Nana who set off 23rd and, roared on by a crowd without Tomba to cheer for the first time in a decade, clocked a time of 1:19.29.
Tomba, who has won four times here and has been on the podium every year a race has been held since 1986, decided to miss the giant after making his season's debut on Tuesday.

The Italian triple Olympic gold medallist suffered a knee and wrist injury in training before the season started and, despite a remarkable second place in Madonna di Campiglio's slalom, felt he was not yet ready for the giant.
Siegfriend Voglreiter and Rainer Salzgeber were Austria's leading hopes for the second leg in fifth and seventh places respectively with times of 1:19.38 and 1:19.48.
Canada's Thomas Grandi was well placed for a career best finish after clocking the sixth fastest time.

Overall World Cup leader Hans Knauss was ninth fastest, ahead of rival Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway in 11th place. Knauss can now be sure of retaining the overall World Cup lead through Christmas after compatriot Thomas Sykora skied out.
Sykora, who beat Tomba in Tuesday's slalom, made an error on the upper part of the piste. Knauss has 371 points in the overall World Cup, Sykora 282 and Aamodt 260.
Norway's Tom Stiansen, winner of a slalom in Breckenridge earlier in the month, lost his balance and missed a gate as did Austria's Christian Mayer.
The second leg, run in reverse 15 order rather than reverse 30, was scheduled to start at 1215 GMT.
